ph_resampling_dists.png: Distance distributions between each 80%-subsample persistence diagram and the FULL-DATA reference diagram (30 deterministic subsamples per shape; H0 and H1 kept separate; bottleneck and Wasserstein, pinned persim 0.4.1; essential class dropped by persim). DESCRIPTIVE resampling stability only: the full-data reference OVERLAPS every subsample, so these are not independent validation; the spread is a variability band, NOT a confidence set; a diagram distance is a metric value, not a hypothesis test. Note the H0 Wasserstein scale is structurally inflated: every subsample has exactly 399 finite H0 classes vs 499 in the reference, and each unmatched short class adds transport cost (the bottleneck, a max, is not affected this way).
ph_resampling_persistence.png: Prominent H1 persistence values across the 30 resamples per shape (solid = resample values, dashed = full-data reference). STABLE features: the annulus dominant loop persistence (1.44-1.58 around the reference 1.496) and the figure-eight co-dominant pair (p1 0.458-0.511, reference 0.481) vary far less than their own scale. VARYING features: the blob's top persistences (no constructed loop; top H1 persistence swings 0.092-0.181 around 0.140) and all noise-scale classes — these have no coherent structure to stabilize. Descriptive stability only; not a confidence set and not a hypothesis test.
ph_resampling_cross_shape.png: Cross-shape comparison of H1 bottleneck distances to the full-data reference (30 resamples per shape; boxes = quartiles, whiskers = range). LEFT: absolute distances. RIGHT: distances divided by each shape's reference dominant H1 persistence — a descriptive scale normalization, not a statistic. The two loop-constructed shapes sit at 2-4% of their dominant persistence; the no-loop blob sits at ~34% of its (noise-scale) top persistence: diagrams of a constructed feature are proportionally far more stable under subsampling than diagrams with no constructed feature. Descriptive only — the reference overlaps each subsample, and no hypothesis test is performed.
mapper_resampling_structure.png: Mapper input-sampling stability: structure statistics of the 30 resample graphs at the FIXED reference parameters (n_cubes=10, overlap=0.35, PCA-1 lens, KMeans k=2 seed 42) — this is NOT the baseline E2 parameter sweep (same data, different parameters); here the data varies and the parameters do not. Node count is 20 in every resample of every shape (2 x n_cubes — the same uninformative pattern as baseline E2, now shown on the input axis). Edges, components and the cyclomatic number (E - V + C: number of independent graph cycles; graph cycles are NOT automatically topological loops) do vary: the annulus reference graph's cycles (cyc=2) disappear (cyc=0) in 13/30 resamples, the figure-eight 2-component reading holds in 24/30, and the no-loop blob is the most variable (cyc 1-6, components 1-3). The custom membership-Jaccard S is NOT shown here because it is an exploratory overlap indicator, not a structural stability measure.
mapper_resampling_graphs_annulus.png: Small multiples for annulus: the full-data reference Mapper graph and the first 6 of the 30 input subsamples, all at the FIXED reference parameters (10, 0.35, PCA-1 lens, KMeans k=2 seed 42). Node size = membership count (global point identities). The graph layout is a RENDERING choice (spring layout, seed 42) — structural comparisons must use the statistics and memberships, not pixel positions. This is input-sampling variation, distinct from baseline E2 parameter sensitivity. Mapper graph cycles are not automatically topological loops (baseline caveat); compare with ph_resampling_persistence.png, where the underlying H1 features remain stable.

The GRAPH is identical in both panels — only the rendering changes (the same distinction the Mapper explorer makes with its layout toggle). weather_loyo.png: Leave-one-calendar-year-out sensitivity of the seasonal-cycle persistent-homology result (Central Park daily TEMP, 2019-2024). Each line is one of the six documented embedding configurations; 'full data' is the saved full-series result; each fold omits one calendar year, re-z-scores the retained days, and builds sliding windows that NEVER cross the gap created by the omitted year (mid-series folds therefore lose 210-630 windows, recorded in weather_loyo.json). FINDING: every fold x configuration retains a dominant H1 class with r_1 >= 4.38 (convention line at 3) — the result does not depend disproportionately on any single observed year. This is a SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS on six years of single-station data: not a population-level climate claim, not a formal confidence interval, not a hypothesis test; a dominant H1 class is consistent with recurrent quasi-periodic structure of the embedded series, not proof of a simple closed physical climate trajectory. r_1 is invariant to the per-fold re-z-scoring; dominant persistence is shown in retained-series z-units.
